name: Halvex
manufacturer: Unknown (military origin suspected; current production: high-end the Gray Zone labs)
description: A classified-origin compound that enables a unique form of one-way sensory and motor data sharing — unlike mutual sync compounds, Halvex allows one user (the 'anchor') to access and partially mirror the augment outputs of a second user (the 'ghost') without the ghost experiencing reciprocal feedback. The anchor can see through the ghost's optical augments, feel through their haptic chrome, and in advanced applications, send motor override signals that influence the ghost's augment movements. Originally theorized as a military command-and-control tool for directing augmented soldiers remotely; the leaked version on the street has obvious applications in surveillance, manipulation, and exploitation.
effects: Anchor gains read access to ghost's augment sensory outputs (vision, haptics, audio)
Anchor can identify ghost's physical location through proprioceptive data
High-dose application: anchor can send motor influence signals to ghost's chrome (ghost experiences as intrusive impulses)
Ghost is unaware of connection unless specifically equipped to detect it
Duration of connection stable across distances up to approximately 2km
side_effects: Anchor: cognitive strain from processing two bodies' worth of sensory data
Anchor: risk of identity confusion — difficulty remembering which body is theirs during long connections
Ghost (if they discover the connection): acute psychological trauma
Both: rare cases of signal feedback if ghost is injured — anchor feels a muted echo of the damage
Anchor: reported intrusive sensory memories from ghost's perspective persisting post-use
street_price: Φ 800-1,500 (anchor dose); ghost dose administered without consent in most street applications
cultural_context: Halvex is genuinely disturbing in its applications and carries a heavy social stigma even in communities where most drugs are accepted. The 'ghost dose' — administered without the victim's knowledge — turns a person's own augments into surveillance equipment and potentially a remote control. On the Gray Zone, it's used by stalkers, abusers, and predators. In the gray market, corporate intelligence operatives use it on unwitting informants. There are whispered accounts of military applications — soldiers directed through hostile environments by commanders experiencing their full sensory feed in real time. The few people who know they've been ghosted without consent describe it as the most profound violation they've experienced.
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone resident has become convinced that someone is ghosting her — her chrome arm keeps making small movements she didn't initiate, and she sees things in her peripheral vision that don't match where she's looking — but no clinic will take her seriously.

A corporate espionage operation collapsed when the ghost asset realized what was happening and deliberately walked into a police station, and now the anchor — still connected and experiencing everything through the asset's augments — is trapped in a feedback loop as the asset is arrested and processed.

A player character discovers that a Halvex anchor dose was slipped to them weeks ago, and someone has been riding their senses ever since — watching through their eyes, listening through their ears, and they need to figure out what was seen before they can understand why they're now being hunted.
